newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria adopts tougher tone against U.S.
newsitem.headline: Syria adopts tougher tone against U.S.

text.p: Syria, angered by what Arabs see as pro-Israeli moves by Washington, has adopted a tough tone against the United States after more than six years of good relations, political analysts say.
Syrian leaders who used to choose mild words when criticising U.S. Middle East policies have begun to condemn the co-sponsor of the Arab-Israeli peace talks in harsh terms, they say.

They cite statements by Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara who blasted Washington late last month for blocking two U.N. resolutions asking Israel to stop building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"The United States protection of Israel at international institutions constitutes one of the irregular phenomena in international ties which does not help spread peace in the world," khaddam told an Islamic conference in Pakistan on March 23. A copy of his speech was obtained by Reuters.

Later Khaddam told a meeting of governors and heads of ruling Baath Party branches of Syrian cities in Damascus that the United States was providing political cover for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "to implement his hardline anti-peace policies".

"The U.S. silence about practices of Netanyahu and providing him with the political cover at the United Nations consituted a negative element in the peace process that weakened America's role as an honest broker of the peace process," Khaddam said. A written copy of his remarks was obtained by Reuters.
Netanyahu who took office last June was condemned by Syria and other Arabs for refusing to swap occupied Arab lands for peace, a principle on which the U.S. peace initiative was based.

His groundbreaking last month for building 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim in East Jerusalem prompted Arab foreign ministers to recommend that Arab states put an end to normal relations with Israel and restore the economic boycott of the Jewish state.
The decison followed violent clashes in the Israeli-occupied territories between Israeli forces and Palestinians protesting against the new settlement building.
Shara accused Washington of trying to protect Israel by sending its Middle East envoy Dennis Ross to the area last week to "rescue Israel from the dilemma created by its anti-peace policies".

"Arabs and Moslems feel the United States seeks to do nothing against Israel when it violates international law or when it makes a mistake. On the contrary the United States rushes to protect Israel as it did when it blocked U.N. draft resolutions demanding a halt to settlement building," Shara said in Morocco on March 28.
Syria's ties with Washington improved dramatically after Damascus joined a U.S.-led multinational force that drove Iraqi froces from Kuwait after seven months of occupation in 1991.
Syria later agreed to a U.S. initiative to engage in peace talks with Israel which opened in Madrid in 1991, although Damascus remained on a U.S. list of countries that allegedly support terrorism.

Syria says it will not resume peace talks with Israel, which broke off a year ago, until Netanyahu accepts the outcome of negotiations held with the previous Labour-led Israeli government which he defeated in elections in May.
Syria says the Labour government agreed during the talks to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
